(Credit: Nomad/PCMag)

In the US, Nomad offers six regular plans: 1GB for $4.50 (seven days), 1GB for $6 (seven days), 3GB for $11 (30 days), 5GB for $14 (30 days), 10GB for $24 (30 days), and 20GB for $35 (30 days). Though they offer the same 1GB of data, the $4.50 and $6.00 plans are indeed different. The $4.50 plan supports AT&T and T-Mobile and starts automatically when connected to a network or after a 30-day window. The $6.00 plan is limited to just AT&T but provides a more flexible 60-day activation window.

Nomad also offers shorter day plans ranging from 1 to 10 days that come with 1GB of high-speed data per day plus unlimited data throttled to 512Kbps. The website and app clearly outline each plan’s details, and all listed prices include applicable taxes.

(Credit: Nomad/PCMag) [...] (Credit: Nomad/PCMag)

Nomad's US pricing is in line with other data-only service providers like Airalo and Saily, which charge $4.50 and $4.39, respectively, for 1GB of data over 7 days.

To use Nomad's eSIM service, your device needs to be unlocked and eSIM compatible. Many modern phones, such as the Apple iPhone 16 and the Samsung Galaxy S24, support eSIMs. If you are unsure if your device will work with Nomad, the company lists the phones, tablets, and laptops that are compatible with its service. [...] Nomad's data-only eSIM is an appealing solution for anyone seeking low-cost data. Its plans and policies are explained in plain language and Nomad's app provides you with almost everything you need to install and manage your eSIM. The installation process could be easier, but on the whole, Nomad works well. That said, we give slight preference to Saily for its easier setup. ### Unlimited Data Plans [...] ### Unlimited Data Plans

Ubigi also offers « Unlimited » plans in select countries like the USA, UK, France, and Japan. It’s important to note these are typically speed-capped unlimited plans (e.g., unlimited data at 4G speeds for the first 1GB per day, then slower speeds). These are excellent for heavy users who prioritize constant connectivity over top-tier speed at all times.

### Practical Pricing Tip

Always compare the regional plan versus individual country plans. If you’re visiting only one or two countries in a region, a single-country plan might be cheaper. If you’re hopping across multiple countries within a defined zone (like the EU), a regional plan offers far better value and convenience.

## Performance and Reliability: What to Expect [...] After a thorough review, Ubigi stands out as a top-tier eSIM provider, particularly for users who value network quality, 5G access, and a polished user experience. Its pricing is transparent and competitive, especially for regional travel in Europe and other zones. The ease of setup—activating a plan from your couch before you even board the plane—cannot be overstated. While it may not always be the absolute cheapest option for every single country, the reliability derived from its robust network partnerships and the convenience of its feature set offers compelling value. For the modern traveler seeking to stay seamlessly connected without the hassle of physical SIM cards, Ubigi delivers a powerful, flexible, and highly effective solution. ## Best Practices for Best eSIM Cards for Europe [...] ## What is Best eSIM Cards for Europe?

The best eSIM cards for Europe are digital SIM cards that allow travelers to stay connected across multiple European countries without the need to swap physical SIM cards. results.content:
### Skinny

Just like Spark and One, Skinny offers a travel SIM option. For $24, you get 2GB of data, 200 texts and minutes to NZ, Australia, and several other countries, valid for 28 days.

Pay $48, and you’ll get 6GB of data, and validity of 60 days. There’s also an $88 data-only version that provides 20GB of data (no calls or texts), again valid for 60 days.

If you don’t want to go with the travel SIM, Skinny’s standard call, data and text packages renew every seven or 28 days. While you can get a very basic monthly package for as little as $8 NZD, the best value is in the larger packs. [...] You’ll get 50GB of data for $79, again valid for three months. This gives unlimited domestic calls and texts as well, plus 200 international minutes/texts to certain countries.

There’s also an unlimited data plan for $129 that lasts three months: your speeds drop dramatically after the first 100GB, however. You’ll also get unlimited domestic calls and texts, and 300 international minutes/texts.

Spark travel SIM/eSIM pricing at Christchurch Airport

A sign on a counter with Spark travel SIM/eSIM pricing at Christchurch Airport [...] Of those, aloSIM has consistently provided the best value for money, so that’s who I’d recommend you go with. That’s not a big surprise: I’ve used them in at least a dozen other countries as well, and they’ve almost always outperformed the competition.

I talk more about speeds and coverage at the end of this article, but for now, suffice it to say that of the three eSIM providers I’ve used (aloSIM, Airalo, and Ubigi), aloSIM had the fastest speeds anywhere and everywhere I’ve tested them.

If you’re new to eSIMs, they offer big benefits to travelers in terms of how quickly, easily, and (often) cheaply you can get connected when you arrive in a new country. Most recent phones support them.
